author: agent
objective: Reconstruct the article's daily climatic-and-pollutant hierarchical-cluster comparison of acute myocardial infarction admissions and in-hospital mortality in metropolitan Sao Paulo.

scientific_invariants.research_question: Reconstruct the article's daily climatic-and-pollutant hierarchical-cluster comparison of acute myocardial infarction admissions and in-hospital mortality in metropolitan Sao Paulo.
scientific_invariants.target_outcome_and_population: Daily acute myocardial infarction admissions and in-hospital mortality among patients admitted in 39 metropolitan Sao Paulo municipalities.
scientific_invariants.principal_contrast: Comparison of daily admissions and in-hospital mortality across the three joint weather-pollution clusters; the abstract identifies high-pollution versus low-pollution clusters as the principal directional comparison.
principal_variants: Daily AMI admissions across weather-pollution clusters
Daily in-hospital AMI mortality across weather-pollution clusters
scientific_invariants.broad_geography: 39 municipalities in metropolitan Sao Paulo, Brazil

article_evidence.finding: The supplied PDF/XML are abstract-only and specify the population, period, DataSUS outcome source, named exposure/weather sources, pollutants, hierarchical clustering, and admissions/mortality comparisons; model details are absent.

article_evidence_map.discrepancy: Supplied materials are not the complete article despite task instruction; full-method details unavailable in supplied corpus.

execution_design.analysis_aggregation: one daily regional time series, joined by admission date; cluster labels derived from z-standardized six daily environmental features
execution_design.assignment_method: fixed Ibirapuera monitor coordinate (-23.592,-46.661) represents a São Paulo municipality feasibility slice; no individual or municipality-wide interpolation
execution_design.coverage_policy: report daily component completeness and retain only complete rows for unsupervised clustering; no arbitrary source threshold
execution_design.daily_aggregation: arithmetic mean of hourly concentration values for each pollutant per local calendar day; weather is provider daily mean/sum
execution_design.exposure_metric: daily NO2, PM2.5, PM10 concentration features plus daily mean temperature, temperature range, precipitation, and mean relative humidity
execution_design.intended_use: bounded source-substitution reanalysis / feasibility reconstruction, not personal exposure or citywide population average
execution_design.source_strategy: public_monitor_network plus documented local atmospheric model fallback for PM10 and weather
execution_design.source: Direct public CETESB legacy hourly-result endpoint (Pinheiros station) for all NO2, PM2.5, and PM10; Open-Meteo archive retained only for daily weather.
execution_design.period: 2014-06-01 through 2014-06-30; June was selected after the predeclared complete-component check showed January 2014 has no monitor PM2.5 observations in the recovered PANGAEA source.

evidence.finding: Public curated hourly Ibirapuera NO2 and PM2.5 records from official CETESB network.
Executable endpoint returns hourly PM10, PM2.5 and NO2 at target coordinate.
Executable endpoint returns daily weather covariates at target coordinate.
Public SIH-RD derivative returned decoded official-field outcome records.

amendments.scientific_justification: The original article lacks monitor-assignment and clustering details, the source's public endpoint has an explicit historical cutoff, and other primary public routes failed. The specified bounded design is fixed before retrieval and will transparently label its limits.

changed_dimensions.period: 2014-06-01 through 2014-06-30; June was selected after the predeclared complete-component check showed January 2014 has no monitor PM2.5 observations in the recovered PANGAEA source.

evidence.finding: January complete-case panel failed because the PANGAEA monitor archive contains zero January 2014 PM2.5 values.
Month-level retained source inspection found both NO2 and PM2.5 observations in June 2014.

amendments.scientific_justification: The source substitution and bounded fixed-location design remain unchanged. Selecting a complete observed month avoids imputing an article-required pollutant and is a deterministic feasibility rule applied before fitting.

changed_dimensions.source: Direct public CETESB legacy hourly-result endpoint (Pinheiros station) for all NO2, PM2.5, and PM10; Open-Meteo archive retained only for daily weather.

evidence.finding: Direct POST to the legacy public result route returned dated Pinheiros hourly tables for NO2, MP10 and MP2.5 on 2014-06-01, with no credential.
Air-quality model route was rejected because its apparent historical values were actually null (the retained diagnostic had a counting mistake); no model concentrations will be used.

amendments.scientific_justification: This is a strictly stronger recovery route than the previously planned monitor archive/model mixture. It preserves the bounded fixed-location/period sensitivity but replaces the failed PM10 model fallback with all three observed pollutants from the article-named regulator.
